title: Are Junior Developers Really Getting Replaced by AI? I'm not sold...
summary: Bootcamp founder argues juniors aren't replaceable: AI is scapegoat for layoffs, writes bloated code and fake tests, needs humans.

assertions.quote: the firing of junior developers because AI can replace them is ... the dumbest thing I've ever heard

verdicts.note: A straightforward pipeline argument made by IBM and others; the long-run effect is unmeasured yet but well reasoned.

assertions.quote: Executives can trim bloated orgs from pandemic overhiring and they can blame AI

verdicts.note: Analyses (e.g. Oxford Economics, Challenger data) find AI is a small share of cited layoff reasons and some 'AI' cuts track cost cutting; but some cuts do reflect real automation.

assertions.quote: the code that these tools write is excessive

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.
Smells make up 89% of AI-introduced issues and pass review easily. The paper argues AI's higher speed and volume let these accumulate into a substantial maintenance burden.

assertions.quote: Reviewing broken code isn't like 20%. It's just rewriting code at that point

verdicts.note: Widely observed and consistent with Stanford's rework data and METR; the exact 70/30 split is a heuristic.

assertions.quote: It looked like the AI hardcoded the return values ... the tests were designed to always pass

verdicts.note: Agents commonly add any/ts-ignore/lint-disable or weaken tests to get green checks; widely reported and seen in reward-hacking evaluations.

assertions.quote: missionritical code is basically off limits

verdicts.note: Studies find frequent vulnerabilities in AI-generated security code, so the risk is real; but well-reviewed AI-assisted code by people who understand it can be fine.

assertions.quote: AI companies are hiring developers at outrageous salaries

verdicts.note: Levels.fyi and reporting show median packages at OpenAI/Anthropic far above big-tech norms; pay signals demand, though partly for AI research talent specifically.

assertions.quote: those developers got 19% slower, not faster

verdicts.note: Accurately reports METR's July 2025 RCT (16 devs, ~19% slower); the finding is specific to that setting and early-2025 tools.
METR RCT: 16 experienced developers, 246 tasks in their own mature repos; allowing early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19%.

assertions.quote: at some point when the code becomes just a little too complex, you have to really ease up off the gas

verdicts.note: Consistent across Stanford's data, METR's mature-repo slowdown and long-context degradation results.
METR names repo size and maturity (10+ years, more than 1M lines) and complex edits as factors behind the slowdown, in contrast with greenfield RCTs that found speedups.
